summary: Verified windowing perf fix on /orders (3696 rows), /company-balance (685 rows), /stock, /stock-arrived and re-ran full backend pytest suite. Windowing works as designed. One regression found: React 'Maximum update depth exceeded' overlay when pressing ArrowDown ~120 times across the window boundary (dev overlay hijacks the page until reload). All other regression flows (autosave, footer counts, scroll to bottom, large paste) pass.

perf_measurements.autosave_flow: typed QAPERF_<ts> into row 3696 -> ALL SAVED indicator shown after 900ms debounce, GET /api/order-rows returns the row, cleanup via blank+id bulk POST returned 200
perf_measurements.keyboard_nav_across_window: 90 ArrowDown from row 0 correctly focused cell-90-party_name and auto-scrolled the grid (scrollTop went to 2464). At 120 presses the React max-update-depth overlay appears (see frontend_issues).

failures_analysed.cause: xdist race - another parallel test (test_same_item_shade_different_group_are_separate_lines) created QA_BAL_G1 stock row between this test's before/after count. Passes when run single-threaded.
xdist race with concurrent balance-stock tests altering QA_AUTO_ITEM stock. Passes single-threaded.

STALE TEST (not a bug). Server now computes to_order = ordered_qty - stock_qty - pending_with_company (see server.py L525). The test still expects to_order == max(0, ordered_qty - stock_qty). Test needs updating, not the code.

minor.issue: backend_test.py::TestCompanyOrder::test_shape_and_totals is stale - it does not account for the pending_with_company subtraction added in the Company Balance flow. Please update the assertion or the test docstring.

ui_bugs.issue: Holding ArrowDown across the window boundary (~90+ presses in a burst, e.g. auto-repeat or keyboard macros) triggers React 'Maximum update depth exceeded'. In dev the webpack-dev-server-client-overlay iframe covers the page and intercepts all clicks until reload; in prod it will spam the console. RCA: focusCell for an off-window row calls setEnsureVisible->scrollToRow which mutates scrollTop imperatively; the ensuing 'scroll' event calls recompute->setRange while setAnchor also calls setSel on every keydown - too many chained state updates within one microtask for React's safety limit. Suggested fix: (a) rAF-throttle recompute in useWindowRows so bursts collapse to one setRange per frame, and/or (b) short-circuit scrollToRow when the row is already within the current [start,end], and/or (c) skip setSel in onKeyDown when the anchor didn't actually move.

issues: Per-keystroke latency is ~100 ms on 3696 rows (median 102, max 124). Fine for typing prose, but sluggish for numeric entry. SheetCell has no React.memo, so every keystroke re-renders all ~560 windowed cells. Consider wrapping SheetCell in React.memo with a shallow prop equality (row-value + row-index) - a cheap 3-5x speed-up.

action_items: Fix Max-update-depth: rAF-throttle useWindowRows.recompute AND skip scrollToRow / setSel when nothing actually changed (this is user-visible in dev).
Add React.memo to SheetCell to bring per-keystroke latency below ~30 ms on 3696-row grids.
Update backend_test.py TestCompanyOrder::test_shape_and_totals so it accounts for pending_with_company subtraction (stale test).
critical_code_review_comments: useWindowRows.recompute writes state on every scroll event without throttling - the scroll listener runs at 60-120Hz during momentum scroll on high-refresh trackpads. Wrap with a requestAnimationFrame guard (single scheduled recompute per frame).

useSheet.focusCell calls ensureRef unconditionally when the element is not in the inputs map; it should first check whether the requested row is inside [win.start, win.end] and only scroll if not - otherwise fresh mounts (during a re-render race) trigger a needless scroll+recompute.
useSheet.onKeyDown calls setAnchor on every ArrowUp/Down/Tab/Enter even when the anchor did not move; combined with 3696 rows this contributes to the burst-key crash.

OrderSheet.jsx line 42-43: blankZeros() replaces `qty: 0/rate: 0` with empty strings when loading, but the normalize() at line 46-52 casts them back to Number(0). The round-trip is fine, but it makes `isBlank` (in useSheet) less robust because empty string vs 0 vs `''` are all treated as blank via .trim() comparison - please add a unit test for this.
Backend server.py list_order_rows uses .to_list(5000) - the DB already has 3696 rows; you are 1.5x away from silently truncating. Either raise the cap or paginate.
seed_data_creation: None. Existing 3696 order rows + 685 CB rows preserved. All QA_/QAPERF_/QAPST_ test rows cleaned up via blank+id bulk delete.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Windowing testids: order-grid, cb-grid, stock-grid, sa-grid. Row-count assertions: document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="order-grid"] input').length should stay <~600 at all scroll positions. To reproduce the Max-update-depth: goto /orders, wait for grid, click any cell in row 0, then send 120 ArrowDown presses with no delay - dev overlay appears. Prod deploy will just spam console.
rca of the issue: Windowing itself is correct (only rows within [start,end] are rendered, pad rows keep scrollHeight = total*33). Max-update-depth chain: onKeyDown(ArrowDown) -> setAnchor->setSel(setState) + focusCell -> off-window -> ensureRef=scrollToRow -> el.scrollTop=... -> synchronous 'scroll' event -> onScroll -> recompute -> setRange(setState) -> re-render -> new scrollToRow identity -> useEffect fires setEnsureVisible (ref, no state) -> next ArrowDown in queue repeats the loop. With 90-120 rapid keydowns Playwright dispatches faster than React can flush, exceeding the default nested-update depth. Fix: rAF-throttle recompute AND early-return scrollToRow when row is already visible.
